sections.p: Thursday's September PPI hit at 8:30 AM ET and ran far hotter than expected: +1.3% m/m (est. 0.6%), core +0.7%, and +6.3% y/y – the biggest gain since 2022 – with retail sales up 0.8% (est. 0.3%). Gold got knocked down to 4,138.10 at 8:35 AM ET as the DXY spiked to 102.26 (8:40 AM ET). The flush didn't last: the 10-year yield rolled over to 5.037% by 10:00 AM ET, AI names took a beating (Nvidia −1.84%, Dell −6.8%), and between 3:00 and 4:00 PM ET gold ripped from 4,157 to 4,176.90. It finished the New York day at 4,170.10 (5:55 PM ET). Anyone who chased the PPI short under 4,140 got squeezed.

Gold opened the overnight session at 4,170.20 at 6:00 PM ET and drifted to the Asian low of 4,147.80 at 9:35 PM ET as the DXY firmed to 102.09 and the 10-year climbed to 5.096%. Buyers came back at 10:20 PM ET: in 35 minutes gold ran from 4,153 to 4,178.30 (10:55 PM ET). Fed Chair Kevin Warsh took the stage at 11:30 PM ET; gold wobbled to 4,163.50 (11:40 PM ET) and bounced right back once it was clear he had nothing new – "I don't prejudge meetings." The Asian high of 4,184.10 came at 12:05 AM ET, right as the DXY bottomed at 101.82. Asia closed at 4,176.50 (2:55 AM ET): high 4,184.10, low 4,147.80, a ~$36 range.

London opened at 4,176.70 at 3:00 AM ET. Gold tagged 4,188.80 at 3:30 AM ET and then a day high of 4,191.30 at 5:15 AM ET. That's where it ran out of gas: the 10-year jumped from 5.073% to 5.102% (4:15 AM ET) and stayed there, and gold slipped to 4,175.20 at 6:05 AM ET – right on the 38.2% retracement of the 4,147.80 → 4,191.30 leg – before bouncing to 4,184. At 6:50 AM ET spot sits near 4,178 (CNBC 4,177.90; gold-api.com 4,178.90), up about $8 from the New York close. The tell: the DXY slid further to 101.58 (6:40 AM ET) and gold didn't follow – yields are in the driver's seat. Neither of this morning's buy setups (4,150–4,160 and 4,160–4,167) filled, and the 4,203–4,212 short never triggered; the dip stopped at 4,175.20. I'd rather miss a move than chase one.

sections.h: Why gold rose – and why it stalled
sections.p: First, a softer dollar: the DXY fell from 102.26 overnight to 101.61 (−0.41% on the day) and is headed for its first weekly loss in five; sterling hit a three-week high on solid UK data (CNBC). That's what lifted gold to 4,191. Second, the Fed: Warsh kept his cards close, so markets still price ~87% odds of an October hold but ~91% odds of a December hike (CME FedWatch via CNBC) – higher-for-longer remains the long-run headwind. Third, yields: the 10-year at 5.102% and the 2-year at 4.751% are still elevated after 3.7% CPI and 6.3% PPI; that's the brake that kept gold under 4,191 even as the dollar fell. Fourth, oil and the war: Brent is near $105.90 with Strait of Hormuz traffic only ~68% of normal (Reuters); President Trump says Iran asked for a halt to strikes and talks are under way, but he hasn't ruled out more (Middle East Eye) – expensive oil keeps inflation fears alive. Fifth, sentiment: the 20 biggest AI and chip stocks have shed more than $1 trillion this week and CoreWeave's five-year CDS briefly topped 1,140 bps (CNBC), yet European stocks are up today (STOXX 600 +0.7%) and the VIX is 16.1 – no panic bid to force a breakout. Longer term, ANZ says a retreat in yields and the dollar would pave the way for gold above $5,000 in 2027 (CNBC).

There's no high-impact U.S. data on Friday's ForexFactory calendar: 8:30 AM ET import prices (est. +0.9%, prior 0.7%), 9:15 AM ET industrial production (+0.4%, prior 0.0%) and capacity utilization (76.5%) – all low impact – plus the federal budget balance at 2:00 PM ET. The Fed enters its blackout period Saturday ahead of the Oct. 27–28 meeting, so today's tape will trade off yields, the dollar, Iran/Hormuz headlines and Friday profit-taking. Level to watch for the weekly close: last Friday's ~4,193.80 – settle above it and the week is green; below it, a small weekly loss (CNBC had gold −0.2% on the week at 4,184).

market_picture_en.text: Gold is caught between two forces today, and yields are winning. A softer dollar – the DXY down to 101.58, a session low and headed for its first weekly loss in five (CNBC) – pushed gold to 4,191. But the 10-year bounced back to 5.10% after a week of hot inflation data (September PPI +6.3% y/y), and FedWatch still prices ~91% odds of a December hike (CNBC) – so the dollar kept falling and gold didn't follow. Warsh gave nothing away and the Fed goes quiet Saturday; Iran/Hormuz risk (Brent near $105.90, Reuters) and the AI-stock rout (CNBC) keep a haven floor under the metal. My view: the primary trend is still up, but as long as the 10-year holds above 5.1%, gold needs to pull back into 4,155–4,165 to reload; only a 4H close above 4,200 opens 4,226 and then 4,300. The play: don't chase 4,185–4,191 – buy the dip.

sections.p: Spot gold was ~4,178 at 2:45 AM ET, dipped only to 4,176.50 (2:55 AM ET) and then ran to a fresh day high of 4,188.80 at 3:30 AM ET as Europe opened. The dollar slid to 101.73 on the DXY (3:35 AM ET) as European stocks opened higher, lifting gold to the day high. The 10-year then climbed from 5.073% to 5.102% (4:15 AM ET), capping bullion under 4,190. No high-impact data in the window.

Right on direction: the up-channel held above 4,170 and price cleared R1 at 4,184 as expected. But there was no dip into the 4,158–4,165 buy zone (low 4,176.50) and no rally into the 4,198–4,208 sell zone (high 4,188.80) – nothing filled, no new TP or stop hits. Earlier closed calls stand in the log: Thursday's London short +21 points, the 6:47 AM ET short +12, the Asian short +21, the New York short −8.

Counterpoints: FedWatch prices about 89% odds of a December hike, and several Indian funds halted bulk gold-ETF subscriptions (CNBC).

sections.h: From the New York afternoon into the Asian open
sections.p: After the hot PPI print, gold flushed to 4,138, popped to 4,167, failed into the U.S. open and was back near 4,145 by 10:17 AM ET. Overnight, softer yields and a softer dollar powered a haven bid straight through prior resistance: Asian session low 4,145.50 at 1:00 PM ET → 4,159 at 3:00 PM ET → Asian high 4,176.90 at 4:00 PM ET (CNBC XAU= day high 4,176.94). From there it has ground lower: 6:00 PM ET 4,169 · 7:00 PM ET 4,163 · 7:50 PM ET 4,157.30 (gold-api.com ~4,158–4,159). December COMEX gold runs about $21.60 over spot.

The 4,177 spike landed right on the 4H BB90 mid/MA89 cluster (4,167 / 4,165) and the 78.6% Fib (4,171) of the 4,197→4,074 down-leg – higher-timeframe supply. The 4H and 3H are still in the lower half of their BB90 (mids 4,167 / 4,158), so the overnight rally was a pullback, not a trend flip. DXY holds near 102.04, the 10-year yield is around 5.08–5.09% (well off its post-CPI peak), Brent ~$105.70 and S&P futures ~7,777 – risk appetite stays cautious with the AI/data-center debt shakeout (CoreWeave CDS) still in play.

The H79 sell signal is already in from the high: price tagged the 4H mid/MA89 sell cluster and the 45m (5:45 / 6:30 / 7:15 PM ET) plus 1H (6:00 / 7:00 PM ET) candles closed red. If you're not in, sell a retrace into 4,165–4,175 (4H BB90 mid 4,167 · 4H MA89 4,165 · Fib 78.6% 4,171 · Asian high cluster 4,172–4,177) only on a red 45m or 1H close – never on a 15m/30m red close alone. Stop at 4,186 (above the 4,177 Asian high and R1 near 4,184). TP1 4,149 (45m mid/MA89), TP2 4,136 (50% Fib of the big down-leg · near the daily pivot at 4,131). A 1H close above 4,186 cancels the short. Buy only at 4,090–4,105 (lower BB90 on the 45m/4H/2H) on a 45m rejection wick with a bullish 45m MACD cross. Fed Chair Warsh speaks at 11:30 PM ET (high impact) – trim size ahead of it.

The 4H (BB90 mid 4,167) and 3H (4,158) sit in the lower half – primary trend down; the 45m/1H/2H briefly tagged the upper half on the overnight pop and are rotating back toward their mids. The 5m/15m/30m up-channel overnight was only a pullback and stalled at the 4H mid/MA89 cluster. MACD histogram: 5m −0.8 · 15m −1.8 · 30m −1.1 · 45m −0.4 (narrowing); 1H still +0.6. RSI(14) is oversold on the 5m (27) and mid-50s on the larger frames. Daily pivots from Oct 15 (H 4,167.10 · L 4,078.60 · C 4,147.60): P 4,131 · R1 4,184 · R2 4,220 · S1 4,095. Fib of the 4,197→4,074 drop: 50% 4,136 · 61.8% 4,150 · 78.6% 4,171 – the 4,177 Asian high sits on the 78.6%.

Vì sao ngược lý thuyết: theo lý thuyết số nóng → USD, lợi suất tăng → vàng giảm, và vàng đúng là giảm 11 giá trong 5 phút đầu. Nhưng thị trường đọc kỹ hơn: phần lớn PPI đến từ năng lượng (chiến tranh Iran đẩy xăng dầu), PPI trừ thực phẩm, năng lượng và thương mại chỉ +0,5%; bán lẻ trừ ô tô và xăng chỉ +0,25% (tháng trước ~1,1%) – người tiêu dùng đang thắt lưng. Lợi suất giảm làm vàng bật lên, dù xác suất Fed tăng lãi tháng 10 lên ~34% (CME FedWatch qua CNBC). Theo phương pháp H79: nhịp bật dừng đúng cụm MA89/BB90 giữa 4H 4.168–4.170, dưới Fib 78,6% 4.171 – giống quy tắc 'nhịp hồi trong xu hướng giảm khựng ở BB giữa khung lớn'. Nhưng sát giờ Mỹ, khẩu vị rủi ro xấu đi: hợp đồng tương lai Nasdaq giảm hơn 1% vì lo các công ty AI vay nợ quá nhiều, S&P 500 tương lai −0,3%. DXY cũng nhích lại từ 102,03 lên 102,13. sections.h: After the 8:30 AM ET data – PPI and retail sales (9:35 AM ET update; 3h filled ~11:37 AM ET)
sections.p: The numbers: September PPI rose 1.3% m/m (est. 0.6%, prior revised to 0.5%) and 6.3% y/y, the biggest annual gain since 2022; core PPI (ex food and energy) +0.7% (est. 0.3%); retail sales +0.8% (est. 0.3%) and ex-autos +0.9% (est. 0.6%). All four beat (BLS, Census via CNBC and Kitco). Spot path (CNBC XAU=, 5-minute bar opens): 3h before, 5:30 AM ET 4,158.60 · 1h before, 7:30 AM ET 4,155.70 · 30 min before, 8:00 AM ET 4,144.50 · release, 8:30 AM ET 4,149.80 · 30 min after, 9:00 AM ET 4,150.30 · 1h after, 9:30 AM ET 4,156.20 · 3h after, 11:30 AM ET 4,154.40 (+0.11%). The release bar flushed to 4,138.10 and snapped back; the post-data high was 4,167.10 at 9:15 AM ET, and spot was back at 4,151.60 by 9:34 AM ET (gold-api.com 4,154.70). Why it went the 'wrong' way: hot data should mean a firmer dollar, higher yields and weaker gold, and gold did drop $11 in the first five minutes. But traders looked under the hood. Energy drove most of the PPI jump as the Iran war keeps fuel prices high; PPI ex food, energy and trade rose just 0.5%, and retail sales ex autos and gas rose only 0.25% after roughly 1.1% in August, a sign consumers are pulling back. Meanwhile the tech selloff (Nasdaq futures −1.3%) pushed money into Treasuries: the 10-year yield fell 14 bps to 5.05% and the DXY slipped 0.5% to 102.07. Lower yields lifted gold even as October hike odds rose to about 34% (CME FedWatch via CNBC). Through the H79 lens: the pop stalled right at the 4H MA89/BB90 mid cluster (4,168–4,170), just under the 78.6% Fib at 4,171, which is the classic downtrend bounce failing at the higher-timeframe mid. Spot sits on the 45m mid (4,150) and below the 1H mid/MA89 (4,158). The 15m/30m channel is still up (price above the MA34/MA89), but both MACDs are below their signal lines and RSI is neutral at 52–58. The short isn't confirmed yet; it needs a red 45m or 1H close back below 4,150. The 8:15 AM ET plan was short 4,158–4,168 (stop 4,178) and long 4,092–4,102 (stop 4,080).

sections.h: From the 6:47 AM ET note into the New York open
sections.p: Gold was at 4,152.50 at 6:47 AM ET. It edged up to 4,158.70 at 7:01 AM ET but couldn't get back to 4,160–4,161 (the 11:00 PM ET Asian high and the 5:35 AM ET London high). Sellers returned from 7:30 AM ET and pushed spot down to 4,144.30 at 8:01 AM ET, just as U.S. desks came online. At 8:17 AM ET spot was 4,149.60 (CNBC XAU= 4,151.66 at 8:19 AM ET; gold-api.com 4,155.30 at 8:21 AM ET), still up about 1.1% on the day. December COMEX gold was 4,169.60, roughly $21.80 over spot.

sections.h: Why gold is where it is
sections.p: The day's tailwinds are still in place: the DXY is at 102.13 (−0.4%), off its 18-month high; the 10-year Treasury yield is at 5.081% (−10.9 bps), around a three-week low; and Brent is at 104.75 (−1.2%). Fed officials Daly and Bowman have signaled no rush to hike at the Oct. 27–28 meeting. But risk appetite soured into the open: Nasdaq futures are down more than 1% on worries about AI companies' heavy borrowing, with S&P 500 futures off 0.3%, and the dollar ticked back up from 102.03 to 102.13. With PPI and retail sales minutes away, longs took profits into the 4,152–4,160 resistance cluster – the BB90 mid on the 45-minute, 2-hour, 3-hour and 1-hour charts.

sections.h: The 8:30 AM ET game plan (PPI + retail sales)
sections.p: Into the data (8:00–8:45 AM ET): no new positions. ForexFactory consensus: PPI +0.6% m/m (prior 0.4%), core PPI +0.3% (prior 0.2%), retail sales +0.3% (prior 1.2%), core retail sales +0.6% (prior 1.4%), alongside jobless claims (199K) and the Philly Fed (28.2). Scenario 1 – hot PPI / strong spending: the dollar and yields pop, gold likely breaks 4,136–4,140 (50% Fib · 30m mid/MA89) and heads to 4,114 (daily pivot), then the 4,092–4,102 buy zone. Scenario 2 – soft PPI / weak spending: gold bounces into 4,158–4,171, which is the high-probability H79 SELL area enter once price is in the zone and a 45m or 1H candle closes red, or a 1H candle pierces above the BB90 mid and closes back below it. Only a 1H close above 4,171 (4H mid, 78.6% Fib) cancels the short and opens 4,197–4,202.

Per the H79 rule, the 45m (BB90 mid 4,152), 1H (4,159), 2H (4,154), 3H (4,159) and 4H (4,170) are all trading in the lower half of their bands – the primary trend is down and the 15m/5m bounce is just a pullback. The 7:15–8:00 AM ET 45m candle tagged the mid area (high 4,158) and closed red at 4,144.80 below it; the 7:00 AM ET 1H candle also closed red at 4,144.80 under its 4,159 mid – the H79 sell confirmation. The 30m and 15m MACD have crossed down (histogram −1.0 / −1.5), while the 45m MACD is still positive but has shrunk from +5.4 to +1.1; RSI(14) is 57 on the 45m and 56 on the 1H – neither overbought nor oversold. Fibonacci of the 4,197 (Oct 13) → 4,074 drop: 50% 4,136, 61.8% 4,150 (where price sits), 78.6% 4,171. Daily pivots: P 4,114 · R1 4,154 · R2 4,202 · S1 4,065.

sections.p: CPI Mỹ tháng 9 ra lúc 19:30 tăng 3,7% so với cùng kỳ, cao hơn dự báo 3,6%, chủ yếu do giá xăng. Vàng đang ở 4.153,7 (19:25) thì bị bán mạnh xuống 4.087 chỉ sau 15 phút, rồi trượt tiếp về 4.074,1 lúc 23:05 – thấp nhất kể từ 7/10. Phiên Mỹ đóng cửa 4.105,2 lúc 04:00, cả ngày 14/10 giảm khoảng 1,3%.

Mở cửa 05:00 ở 4.104, giá dò xuống đáy Á 4.099,9 lúc 06:05 rồi bật mạnh từ 07:10: chỉ trong 10 phút vàng vọt từ 4.116 lên 4.142, đúng lúc bài phỏng vấn của bà Daly (Fed San Francisco) được đăng – Fed có thể còn phải tăng lãi nhưng không cần vội ở tháng 10. Nhịp thứ hai 09:45–10:00 đưa giá lên đỉnh Á 4.161,1 lúc 10:00, cùng lúc DXY chạm đáy 101,88. Sau đỉnh, lực chốt lời kéo giá về 4.131,9 lúc 13:00; phiên Á đóng 4.135,7 – vẫn tăng khoảng 32 giá so với mở cửa.

Mở 14:00 ở 4.136, giá đi lên đều: vượt 4.150 lúc 15:00–15:15 và lên đỉnh 4.160,2 lúc 16:35 – thấp hơn đỉnh Á đúng 1 giá. Cả hai lần chạm 4.160–4.161 đều bị bán xuống. Lúc 17:50 giá quanh 4.154 (gold-api.com 4.155,5–4.156 lúc 17:59–18:00), tăng khoảng 49 giá (+1,2%) so với giá chốt hôm qua 4.105. Như vậy vàng đã lấy lại toàn bộ cú rơi sau CPI.

Thứ nhất, USD hạ nhiệt: DXY từ 102,53 đầu phiên Á xuống 102,06 (−0,5%), rời đỉnh 18 tháng lập hôm qua. Thứ hai, lợi suất 10 năm Mỹ còn 5,085% (−10,5 điểm cơ bản), thấp nhất 3 tuần, 2 năm 4,74% – tiền trú ẩn chảy vào trái phiếu khi cổ phiếu công nghệ châu Á bị bán tháo. Thứ ba, Fed bớt diều hâu: Daly nói chưa cần tăng lãi ở cuộc họp 27–28/10, Bowman muốn chờ thêm; FedWatch còn khoảng 29% khả năng tăng lãi tháng 10, từ mức 50% ngay sau CPI. Thứ tư, dầu giảm: Brent từ 106 về 104,6 (đáy 103,4 lúc 15:20) khi Mỹ tính nới trừng phạt nhóm tàu chở dầu bị cấm vận, dù eo Hormuz vẫn nóng – tàu GFS Pride của Singapore bị đánh chìm, Iran dọa tấn công tàu chiến Mỹ. Dầu hạ bớt lo lạm phát. Dù vậy, Ole Hansen (Saxo) vẫn cho rằng bức tranh kỹ thuật của vàng còn mong manh.

19:30: PPI tháng 9 (dự báo +0,6% m/m, kỳ trước 0,4%), PPI lõi (+0,3%, trước 0,2%), doanh số bán lẻ (+0,3%, trước 1,2%) và bán lẻ lõi (+0,6%, trước 1,4%) – cả bốn đều là tin đỏ trên ForexFactory; cùng giờ có đơn trợ cấp thất nghiệp (dự báo 199K) và chỉ số Philly Fed (28,2). PPI nóng cộng bán lẻ mạnh sẽ kéo USD và lợi suất bật lại, vàng dễ mất nhịp hồi; PPI mềm có thể giúp vàng thử lại vùng 4.160–4.171. 10:30 sáng mai (16/10) Chủ tịch Fed Warsh phát biểu tại hội nghị IMF – World Bank, cũng là tin đỏ.

Giá 4.154 vừa nhích lên trên BB90 giữa 45m (4.151) và MA89 (4.151), MA34 còn thấp ở 4.122; dải trên 4.211, dải dưới 4.091. MACD 45m dương nhưng histogram thu hẹp dần (+7,9 lúc 10:45 xuống +2,4), RSI14 61 – lực hồi đang yếu đi. Khung lớn: BB90 giữa 1H 4.160 (MA89 4.159), 3H 4.159 và 4H 4.171 (MA89 4.170) vẫn nằm trên giá, 2H đứng sát giữa 4.154 → xu hướng chính vẫn giảm. Bộ lọc H79: 15m kênh tăng (giá > MA34 4.147 > MA89 4.121), 5m dẹt quanh MA34 4.155, 30m chưa thành kênh tăng (MA34 4.130 còn dưới MA89 4.141) → đây là nhịp hồi trong xu hướng giảm, dễ dừng ở cụm BB giữa/MA89 khung lớn 4.159–4.171. Tín hiệu BÁN đẹp: giá vào 4.160–4.170 — vào khi giá vào vùng bán và có nến 45m hoặc 1H đóng đỏ xác nhận, hoặc nến 1H đâm xuyên lên BB giữa rồi đóng lại dưới band (dưới 4.160), chắc hơn khi 45m đóng dưới BB giữa 4.151.

sections.p: September CPI landed at 8:30 AM ET Wednesday at 3.7% y/y, above the 3.6% consensus, driven mostly by gasoline. Gold was at 4,153.70 at 8:25 AM ET and got hit down to 4,087 within 15 minutes, then slid to 4,074.10 at 12:05 PM ET – its lowest since Oct. 7. It settled at 4,105.20 at 5:00 PM ET, down about 1.3% on the day.

Gold opened at 4,104 at 6:00 PM ET and dipped to the Asian low of 4,099.90 at 7:05 PM ET before ripping higher from 8:10 PM ET: in ten minutes it ran from 4,116 to 4,142 as San Francisco Fed President Mary Daly's interview hit the wires – more hikes are likely, but there's no rush in October. A second leg at 10:45–11:00 PM ET carried it to the Asian high of 4,161.10 at 11:00 PM ET, right as the DXY bottomed at 101.88. Profit-taking pulled it back to 4,131.90 by 2:00 AM ET, and Asia closed at 4,135.70 – still up about $32 from the open.

London opened at 4,136 at 3:00 AM ET and gold climbed steadily, clearing 4,150 at 4:00–4:15 AM ET and peaking at 4,160.20 at 5:35 AM ET – exactly a dollar shy of the Asian high. Both runs at 4,160–4,161 were sold. At 6:50 AM ET gold was hovering near 4,154 (gold-api.com 4,155.50–4,156 at 6:59–7:00 AM ET), up about $49 (+1.2%) from yesterday's 4,105 settle. In other words, the entire post-CPI drop has been erased.

First, the dollar cooled: the DXY slipped from 102.53 at the Asian open to 102.06 (−0.5%), backing off Wednesday's 18-month high. Second, the 10-year Treasury yield fell to 5.085% (−10.5 bps), a three-week low, with the 2-year at 4.74% – haven money rotated into bonds as Asian tech stocks sold off. Third, the Fed sounded less hawkish: Daly sees no need to hike at the Oct. 27–28 meeting and Bowman wants to wait; FedWatch now shows about 29% odds of an October hike, down from 50% right after CPI. Fourth, oil eased: Brent dropped from 106 to 104.60 (low of 103.40 at 4:20 AM ET) as Washington weighs easing sanctions on 'shadow fleet' tankers, even though Hormuz remains hot – Singapore's GFS Pride was sunk and Iran threatened U.S. warships. Cheaper oil takes some heat off inflation fears. Still, Saxo's Ole Hansen calls gold's technical outlook fragile.

8:30 AM ET: September PPI (est. +0.6% m/m, prior 0.4%), core PPI (+0.3%, prior 0.2%), retail sales (+0.3%, prior 1.2%) and core retail sales (+0.6%, prior 1.4%) – all four high-impact on ForexFactory – plus initial jobless claims (est. 199K) and the Philly Fed index (est. 28.2). A hot PPI with strong spending would lift the dollar and yields and likely cap the bounce; a soft print could send gold back to test 4,160–4,171. Fed Chair Kevin Warsh speaks at 11:30 PM ET at the IMF–World Bank meetings, another high-impact event.

At 4,154, gold has just edged above the 45m BB90 mid (4,151) and MA89 (4,151), with MA34 well below at 4,122; upper band 4,211, lower band 4,091. The 45m MACD is positive but the histogram keeps shrinking (+7.9 at 11:45 PM ET to +2.4) and RSI(14) sits at 61 – the bounce is losing steam. Higher timeframes: the BB90 mid on the 1H (4,160, MA89 4,159), 3H (4,159) and 4H (4,171, MA89 4,170) all sit above price, with the 2H right at its mid (4,154) – the primary trend is still down. H79 filter: the 15m is in an up-channel (price > MA34 4,147 > MA89 4,121), the 5m is flattening around MA34 4,155, and the 30m has not confirmed (MA34 4,130 still below MA89 4,141) – a pullback inside a downtrend that tends to stall at the higher-timeframe mid/MA89 cluster at 4,159–4,171. Daily pivots: P 4,114 · R1 4,154 · R2 4,202 · S1 4,065. Fibonacci of the 4,197 (Oct 13) → 4,074 drop: 50% 4,136, 61.8% 4,150 (already cleared), 78.6% 4,171 – matching the 4H mid. The clean SELL setup: price in 4,160–4,170 enter once price is in the zone and a 45m or 1H candle closes red, or a 1H candle pierces above the BB90 mid and closes back below it (under 4,160), stronger still on a 45m close below the 4,151 mid.

sections.p: Từ 13:45 vàng giao ngay ~4.136 đi lên đều, vượt 4.150 khoảng 15:00 và chạm đỉnh ~4.160 lúc 15:25 – đúng mép dưới vùng bán 4.155–4.168. Sau đó giá bị đẩy về ~4.151–4.153 lúc 15:55. Hai giờ đầu phiên Âu vàng tăng ~16 giá.

USD và lợi suất Mỹ tiếp tục lùi: DXY ~102,06 (−0,5%), lợi suất 10 năm ~5,09% (−10 điểm cơ bản) theo CNBC. Brent giảm ~2% về ~103,8 USD dù Hormuz vẫn nóng (tàu Singapore bị đánh chìm, Iran dọa tàu chiến Mỹ), vì Mỹ tính nới trừng phạt tàu chở dầu. Chứng khoán châu Âu mở cửa giảm theo đợt bán công nghệ ở châu Á – tiền chạy vào trái phiếu.

Lợi suất và USD giảm làm vàng hấp dẫn hơn. Các quan chức Fed Daly và Bowman nói chưa cần tăng lãi ngay tháng 10, nên cược tăng lãi hạ xuống (FedWatch ~27% theo CNBC/Reuters). Dầu giảm cũng bớt lo lạm phát. Lực mua đủ đẩy giá hồi, nhưng chưa đủ phá cụm BB giữa.

Đúng kịch bản: chờ hồi lên BB giữa để bán. Giá hồi lên ~4.160 và chững ngay dưới cụm BB giữa 45m/2H (~4.155), trùng Fib 50–61,8% sóng giảm 4.224 → 4.073 (~4.149–4.166). Lệnh bán khớp mép dưới vùng, chưa tới TP1 4.140, SL 4.178 chưa chạm. Vùng mua 4.097–4.110 không khớp.

45m–4H vẫn dưới BB giữa nên xu hướng chính là giảm; 15m kênh tăng chỉ là nhịp hồi. Nến 45m 14:30 đóng sát trên BB giữa, nến 15:15 đang đỏ quay lại dưới – nếu nến đóng 16:00 giữ dưới ~4.155 là tín hiệu bán H79 rõ hơn. MACD 45m vẫn dương nên vào khối lượng nhỏ. Trước tin dễ giằng co 4.140–4.165.

19:30 PPI (dự báo 0,6% m/m, lõi 0,3%) và bán lẻ (0,3%). Không vào lệnh mới 19:00–19:45. PPI nóng → USD, lợi suất bật → vàng dễ quay về 4.140 rồi 4.125, sâu hơn là vùng mua 4.097–4.110. PPI mềm → vàng có thể thử 4.168–4.178; nến 1H đóng trên 4.175 thì bỏ lệnh bán. Sau tin chỉ bán khi giá vào vùng bán và có nến 45m hoặc 1H đóng đỏ xác nhận, hoặc nến 1H đâm xuyên lên BB giữa rồi đóng lại dưới band; nếu đóng trên thì đứng ngoài phiên.

sections.p: From 2:45 AM ET, spot gold climbed steadily from ~4,136, cleared 4,150 around 4:00 AM ET and hit ~4,160 at 4:25 AM ET – right at the bottom of the 4,155–4,168 sell zone. It then slipped back to ~4,151–4,153 by 4:55 AM ET, about +16 points over the first two hours of London.

The dollar and Treasury yields kept easing: DXY ~102.06 (−0.5%), U.S. 10-year ~5.09% (−10 bps), per CNBC. Brent fell ~2% to ~$103.8 even as Hormuz stays tense (a Singapore ship sunk, Iran threatening U.S. warships), as Washington weighs easing tanker sanctions. European stocks opened lower after Asia's tech selloff, sending money into bonds.

Lower yields and a softer dollar made bullion more attractive. Fed officials Daly and Bowman signaled no rush to hike in October, trimming hike bets (FedWatch ~27%, per CNBC/Reuters). Cheaper oil also eased inflation worries. Buyers lifted gold into the bounce but couldn't clear the mid-band cluster.

On script: the plan was to sell a bounce into the mid-band. Gold rallied to ~4,160 and stalled just under the 45m/2H BB mid (~4,155), overlapping the 50–61.8% retracement of the 4,224 → 4,073 drop (~4,149–4,166). Shorts filled at the bottom of the zone; TP1 4,140 not hit yet, stop 4,178 untouched. The 4,097–4,110 buy zone did not fill.

45m through 4H remain below the BB mid, so the primary trend is down; the 15m up-channel is just a pullback. The 3:30 AM ET 45m candle closed right above the mid-band, and the 4:15 AM ET candle is red back below it – a close under ~4,155 at 5:00 AM ET would firm up the H79 sell signal. The 45m MACD is still positive, so keep size small. Expect chop between 4,140 and 4,165 into the data.

PPI (est. +0.6% m/m, core +0.3%) and retail sales (est. +0.3%) at 8:30 AM ET. No new trades 8:00–8:45 AM ET. A hot PPI lifts the dollar and yields → gold likely back to 4,140, then 4,125, with the 4,097–4,110 buy zone below. A soft print could test 4,168–4,178; a 1-hour close above 4,175 cancels the short. After the release, sell only — enter once price is in the zone and a 45m or 1H candle closes red, or a 1H candle pierces above the BB90 mid and closes back below it; a close above it means sit the session out.

sections.p: Tuesday's US session sold gold off from 4,193 (8:30 AM ET) to 4,148 (1:50 PM ET), settling near 4,162 – a second straight down day, roughly 0.8% lower over two sessions.

Gold opened at 4,163 at 6:00 PM ET and slipped to the Asian low of 4,145 at 9:45 PM ET before bouncing to the Asian high of 4,172 at 11:15 PM ET – about five hours after the open – on dovish comments from the NY Fed's Williams. Sellers then picked the prior move back up, and Asia closed at 4,149.
High of 4,159 at 4:15 AM ET, low of 4,141 at 6:25 AM ET – the low of the day. Heading into 7:00 AM ET, gold was hovering around 4,138–4,144.

A slightly softer dollar (DXY ~102.1) and long-end Treasury yields down 3–4 bps kept the slide contained. But Brent above $106 on renewed Middle East attacks revived inflation worries. Williams sees one more hike this year but none in 2027, while Waller and Goolsbee leaned hawkish on AI-driven price pressure. Markets price roughly 90% odds of a December hike – higher rates remain the main headwind for gold.
September CPI at 8:30 AM ET: headline est. 3.6% y/y; core est. +0.2% m/m and 2.5% y/y. A hot print would lift the dollar and yields and pressure gold; a soft one would support a bounce.

Price is below MA34 (4,162) and MA89 (4,176), hugging the lower BB90 (2 SD) at 4,142 (mid 4,176, upper 4,211). Daily pivots: P 4,171 · R1 4,194 · S1 4,139 · S2 4,116. Into the NY open, expect chop between 4,139 and 4,163 until CPI: a hot core print could break S1 toward 4,116; a soft one could lift price back to 4,162–4,171.
